prompt.context: Client Co. manufactures wooden boards installed on walls of houses and is thinking about entering the Hot Tiles product category. Hot Tiles are tiles used to make BBQ decks in the backyards of houses. They want us to help them understand if they should enter this market.
prompt.question: Should Client Co. enter the Hot Tiles market? Specifically, can they achieve their expansion target of $1B in Year 1 sales?

clarifying_info.q: How long has the client been in business and where do they operate?
clarifying_info.a: Client has been in the house-board business for 20 years in the US only.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's revenue or growth target?
clarifying_info.a: Expansion target is $1B in sales in Year 1; profitability is not a focus.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the competitors in the Hot Tile segment?
clarifying_info.a: No direct competitor data in the Hot Tile segment. There are substitute tile products in the market called Super Hot Tiles.

clarifying_info.q: How does the client currently sell its products?
clarifying_info.a: Client Co currently sells house-boards through big box retailers such as Walmart, Home Depot, Costco, etc.

clarifying_info.q: What percentage of US households live in a house with a backyard?
clarifying_info.a: 50% of US households live in a house with a backyard (not in high-rises, apartments, condos, etc.).

clarifying_info.q: What share of households with houses already have BBQ decks?
clarifying_info.a: 30% of households with houses have existing BBQ decks.

clarifying_info.q: How often do existing BBQ deck owners replace their tiles?
clarifying_info.a: Replacement period for households with existing BBQ decks is 15 years.

clarifying_info.q: What is the expected conversion rate for new customers?
clarifying_info.a: Expected conversion rate of new customers (households with houses and no existing BBQ deck) is 1%.

clarifying_info.q: What is the price per tile?
clarifying_info.a: Price per tile is $100 per sqft. Tile dimensions are 1ft x 0.5ft.

exhibits.title: Historical sales of Hot Tile vs Super Hot Tiles
exhibits.shows: A table showing annual unit sales figures for Hot Tiles and Super Hot Tiles from 2013 to 2017.

exhibits.title: Manufacturing utilization rates
exhibits.shows: A chart showing manufacturing utilization rates across Plant 1, Plant 2, and Plant 3 over time, with notes that Plant 1 had a large capacity expansion in 2016, Plant 2 is the central hub for house-board products absorbing increasing regional sales, and Plant 3 caters to regions with lower house sales.
exhibits.data: Plant 1: significant unused capacity post-2016 expansion; Plant 2: high utilization; Plant 3: lower utilization

framework: Market sizing: estimate total addressable market for Hot Tiles in the US and assess whether $1B (15% share) is achievable
Demand-side levers: existing BBQ deck replacement customers, new customers converting to BBQ decks, market penetration vs substitutes
Supply-side levers: raw materials sourcing, manufacturing capacity, distribution channels, branding and marketing
Risk assessment: product characteristics (discretionary, high-price), competitive dynamics with Super Hot Tiles, macro environment

questions.prompt: How large is the total addressable market for Hot Tiles in the US?
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a bottom-up market size: start with population, derive households, filter to houses with backyards, split into existing-deck and new-deck segments, apply replacement rate and conversion rate, adjust for substitute tile penetration, then multiply by average deck price. Strong candidates will articulate each assumption before calculating and note that Super Hot Tiles capture ~75% of the addressable market.

math.setup: Population 300M -> 100M households (3 persons/HH) -> 50M HH in houses with backyard. Of those, 30% (15M) have existing BBQ decks and 70% (35M) do not. Annual demand from old customers = 15M / 15-year replacement = 1M. Annual demand from new customers = 35M * 1% conversion = 0.35M. Total = 1.35M customers. Adjust for Hot Tile share of market (25% based on Exhibit 1 ratio) = 1.35M * 25% = ~340K. Avg deck = 10ft x 10ft = 100 sqft; tile = 1ft x 0.5ft = 0.5 sqft; #tiles = 200; price = $100/sqft so cost per tile = $100 * 0.5 = $50 but price is stated as $100/sqft -> total price per deck = 100 sqft * $100/sqft = $10,000... re-check: raw text says Total price = 200 * $100 = $20,000 (treating $100 as price per tile unit, not per sqft in final calc). Use casebook figures.
steps: Hot Tile market share vs substitutes = 25% (from Exhibit 1: Hot Tiles ~25% of combined sales)
math.answer: Total addressable market is approximately $6.8B. Client Co needs ~15% market share to hit its $1B target.

questions.prompt: What does Exhibit 1 tell us about the Hot Tiles market relative to Super Hot Tiles, and what does this imply for our market sizing?
questions.guidance: Candidate should observe that Super Hot Tiles consistently outsell Hot Tiles by roughly 3:1 across all years. This implies Hot Tiles capture only about 25% of the combined market. Candidate should apply this ratio to narrow down the addressable customer base. Stronger candidates will also probe why Super Hot Tiles have higher sales (broader applications due to greater heat resistance) and consider competitive implications.

math.setup: Ratio of Hot Tiles to total (Hot + Super Hot) sales each year.
steps: Average ~25%; equivalently Super Hot Tiles have ~3x the sales of Hot Tiles
math.answer: Hot Tiles represent approximately 25% of the combined Hot + Super Hot Tile market. Apply 25% factor to total addressable customer pool.

questions.prompt: Walk through the operational value chain. What levers determine whether 15% market share is achievable?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure analysis across: (1) Raw Materials - same wood as current products, minor incremental cost for heat-resistant engineering layer; (2) Manufacturing - Plant 1 has spare capacity post-2016 expansion and can produce both tiles and boards; (3) Distribution - existing big-box retailer relationships (Walmart, Home Depot, Costco) provide immediate channel access; (4) Marketing/Branding - strong existing brand known for reliability; brand loyalty can support launch.

questions.prompt: What are the key risks and product characteristics the client should be aware of before entering?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: (1) High unit price ($20K per deck) makes this a discretionary, big-ticket purchase subject to macro volatility; (2) Post-housing-market-crash sensitivity - consumers' propensity to spend on high-value household assets is low; (3) Competition from Super Hot Tiles which have broader applications (more heat resistant); (4) Demographic risk - millennial preference patterns (lower home/car ownership) may reduce the addressable market over time.

brainstorming.prompt: What levers should be analyzed to understand if 15% market share is feasible, drawing on the operational value chain?

categories.name: Raw Materials
ideas: Raw materials (wood) are the same as current house-board products
Existing supplier relationships can be leveraged
An extra layer of heat-resistant engineering is required but cost is relatively small
Negotiating bulk supply agreements can keep upstream costs low

categories.name: Manufacturing
ideas: Plant 1 has significant spare capacity after a 2016 capacity expansion
Same factories can produce both tiles and housing boards
Plant 2 is focused on house boards and should not be reallocated
Plant 3 serves low-demand regions and is less suitable for BBQ-deck-heavy markets

categories.name: Distribution
ideas: Existing big-box retailer relationships (Walmart, Home Depot, Costco) provide immediate shelf access
Bundle Hot Tiles with existing house-board products at point of sale
Leverage current sales force and logistics network

categories.name: Marketing / Branding
ideas: Strong brand image with reputation for reliability
Brand loyalty from existing house-board customers can reduce customer acquisition cost
Potential to bundle products at point of sale to cross-sell to existing customer base
Develop service strategy for old customers to shorten replacement cycle from 15 years

categories.name: Demand Stimulation
ideas: Target new customers (households with houses but no BBQ deck) with promotional pricing
Investigate differentiation vs Super Hot Tiles on quality, design, or price
Explore product extensions or customization to capture premium segment

recommendation: Recommend Client Co. enter the Hot Tile business
Total addressable market is approximately $6.8B; the $1B target requires only ~15% market share

Client Co. has strong operational fit: same raw materials, available manufacturing capacity at Plant 1, existing big-box distribution relationships, and a trusted brand — all of which make 15% share achievable
risks: High unit price (~$20K per deck) makes this a discretionary, high-volatility purchase sensitive to macroeconomic conditions
Post-housing-market-crash environment may suppress consumer spending on big-ticket home improvements
Super Hot Tiles are a strong substitute with broader heat-resistant applications and ~3x the current market share
Millennial homeownership trends may compress the long-term addressable market
next_steps: Understand key differentiation between Hot Tiles and Super Hot Tiles (product quality, heat resistance, price) to sharpen positioning
Close agreements with raw material partners to lock in upstream costs
Develop branding and marketing strategy for new customers, potentially bundling products at point of sale
Develop a service and loyalty strategy for existing deck owners to shorten the 15-year replacement cycle
